verdict_reason: Only 4 tiles were on the sheet (the pile is listed as 12 photos / 7 photographers, so this is a small sample of it), and all 4 - from 4 different photographers - are the same place. 7684726926 shows the Tran Ba Dinh pavilion on the Ngoc Son island: square grey stone columns carrying vertical Han inscriptions, red timber posts and red lanterns, a curtain of banyan aerial roots overhead, bonsai on the flagstones, and Hoan Kiem Lake with its far shore straight through the open sides, behind the island's white-and-red pierced balustrade. 8124565618 is a Ngoc Son gate: grey rendered arch with a circular moon opening, ceramic dragon roof finials, and legible Han couplets on the piers (left reads 'thuy sac son quang tuong tong nghinh'), with a yellow interpretive board mounted inside the archway and the same white pierced balustrade below. 9413604918 is the sculpted white-and-gold tiger relief on that gate's rockwork wall (Ngoc Son's tiger, the pair to its dragon). Because four unrelated photographers independently land on one temple island, this pin is a real subject, not a centroid - though the sample is small.

photos.evidence: Open temple pavilion on a lake terrace: square grey stone columns with vertical Han inscriptions cut into them, red-painted timber posts and beams, red silk lanterns, a dense curtain of banyan aerial roots hanging from the tree above, bonsai in ceramic pots and stone tables on cobbled paving, families sitting on the low brick seat - and behind the white-and-red pierced balustrade, Hoan Kiem Lake with its wooded far bank and city buildings. This is the Tran Ba Dinh pavilion on the Ngoc Son island.

Grey rendered temple gate with a single arch, a circular 'moon' opening above it in a panel of carved cloud scrolls, a curved pantile roof with pale ceramic dragon finials and a small inscribed plaque at the upper left. White boards on both piers carry legible Han couplets - the left one reads 水色山光相送迎 - and gilt ornaments flank the arch. A yellow interpretive board is fixed to the wall inside the archway, and a white balustrade of square pierced panels runs across the bottom of the frame: the same balustrade type as the confirmed Ngoc Son island terrace in 7684726926.

Temple altar bay: a tall gilded openwork shrine frame on red-lacquered columns enclosing three seated deity figures (a gold figure, a yellow-robed scholarly figure and a green-robed martial figure), with offerings of lilies, gladioli, Buddha's-hand citron and stacked votive boxes in front. A red banner at the right carries gold characters beginning with 文 (van), consistent with a Van Xuong altar such as Ngoc Son's, but no full inscription or exterior view is visible, so this is a weak attribution.

Close-up of a life-size sculpted tiger relief - white body with gold-ochre stripes, heavy black eye and whisker markings, red mouth - modelled walking out of a dark grey rockwork wall with painted green foliage tufts. Matches the tiger relief on the Ngoc Son gate that pairs with its dragon relief; a temple tiger relief alone is not unique in Hanoi, so I am not treating this as proof on its own.
